title: Pistachio barfi
subtitle: Indian pistachio milk fudge
excerpt: Barfi is a dense Indian confection made by reducing milk solids with sugar until the mixture holds a firm but yielding slab. The pistachio version gets its colour from blended raw pistachios folded into condensed milk solids. It slices cleanly, tastes richly of pistachio and cream, and keeps well, it's the kind of sweet that improves after a day in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Barfi (also spelled burfi or burfee) is one of the oldest fudge-type sweets on the South Asian subcontinent, appearing in regional variations from Rajasthan to Bengal. The core technique, reducing milk solids with sugar to a firm slab, is also found in the Middle East and Central Asia under different names. The pistachio version is associated with Rajasthani and Lucknow sweet shops (mithai shops) and is a staple of Diwali gift boxes across the diaspora. Traditional recipes used freshly made khoya; condensed milk is the practical home equivalent.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 2 hours ahead to allow the slab to firm up fully before cutting.

content.text: Pistachio barfi is a dense, lightly sweet milk fudge with a clean pistachio flavour and a pale green colour. The mixture cooks down on the hob until it pulls away from the pan, then sets in a tin. No thermometer is needed, you read the texture of the mixture rather than its temperature. Chilling firms the slab enough to cut clean squares.

Put 150 g of the pistachios in a food processor and blitz to a coarse paste. Add 2 tablespoons of the condensed milk and blitz again until the mixture forms a finer paste that clumps when pressed. Set aside.

Melt the ghee in a medium saucepan over a low to medium heat. Add the remaining condensed milk and stir to combine. Add the milk powder a few tablespoons at a time, stirring after each addition until absorbed. Once all the milk powder is in, add the pistachio paste and the cardamom. Stir continuously over a medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes. The mixture will stick and stiffen; keep scraping the base and sides of the pan with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula. It is ready when it pulls cleanly away from the pan sides and the base, forms a mass, and no longer sticks to the spoon.

Line a 20 cm square baking tin with parchment paper. Tip the mixture into the tin and press flat with the back of a spoon or a lightly oiled piece of parchment. The layer should be about 1.5 cm deep. Scatter the chopped pistachios over the top and press them gently into the surface. Leave to cool to room temperature, about 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 1 further hour until fully firm.

Lift the slab out of the tin using the parchment. Cut into 16 squares with a sharp knife, wiping the blade clean between cuts. The barfi keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
